ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The package circulation route in the logistics park is shown in the figure. The inclined plane $AB$ has a length $L=2.5\mathrm{m}$ and an inclination angle $\theta=37^{\circ}$. A package with mass $m=2\mathrm{kg}$ slides down from rest at point $A$ on the inclined plane. After passing through a negligible smooth small arc at the bottom of the inclined plane, it slides onto a horizontal conveyor belt at point $B$. The conveyor belt rotates clockwise at a constant speed. Once the package reaches the same speed as the conveyor belt, it flies horizontally off the end of the conveyor belt at point $C$ and finally lands in a packaging box on the ground. The vertical height between the packaging box and point $C$ is $h=0.8\mathrm{m}$, and the horizontal distance is $s=1.6\mathrm{m}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the package and the inclined plane is $\mu_{1}=0.65$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the package and the conveyor belt is $\mu_{2}=0.2$. Take $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, and $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$. Find:

1. What is the magnitude of the velocity \( v_{1} \) when the package slides onto the conveyor belt at point \( B \)?
2. What is the speed $v_{2}$ of the conveyor belt moving at a constant velocity?
3. What is the heat $Q$ generated by friction between the package and the conveyor belt?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an inclined plane; the block slides down from the upper end A of the inclined plane along AB to B; from B to C is a horizontal conveyor belt, and above the conveyor belt at C there is an arrow pointing to the right, indicating that the upper surface moves to the right; after the block reaches C, it flies out horizontally to the right, the dashed trajectory indicates projectile motion, the vertical height from C to the ground point E below is marked as h, and the horizontal distance from E to the packaging box position D is marked as s. Calculate according to the specified method: 1. For the inclined-plane section, use the kinetic energy theorem: the initial speed is 0, gravity does work mgL sinθ along the inclined plane, and friction does negative work μ1 mg cosθ · L, so (1/2)mv1^2 = mgL sinθ − μ1 mg cosθ · L. Canceling m gives v1^2 = 2gL(sinθ − μ1 cosθ) = 2×10×2.5×(0.6 − 0.65×0.8). 0.65×0.8=0.52, so v1^2=50×0.08=4, v1=2 m/s. 2. After flying out from C, it undergoes horizontal projectile motion. In the vertical direction h=(1/2)gt^2, that is, 0.8=5t^2, giving t^2=0.16, t=0.4 s. In the horizontal direction s=v2 t, so v2=s/t=1.6/0.4=4 m/s. 3. On the conveyor belt, the upper surface of the conveyor belt is to the right and its speed is 4 m/s, greater than the 2 m/s when the block has just reached B, so the friction force accelerates the block to the right. The friction force f=μ2mg=0.2×2×10=4 N, and the acceleration a=f/m=4/2=2 m/s^2. The time required for the block to accelerate from v1=2 m/s to v2=4 m/s is tb=(v2−v1)/a=(4−2)/2=1 s. In this process, the block's displacement x_pkg=(v1+v2)tb/2=(2+4)×1/2=3 m, and the conveyor-belt surface displacement x_belt=v2 tb=4×1=4 m. The relative sliding distance is x_belt−x_pkg=1 m, so the heat generated by friction Q=f·Δx=4×1=4 J.
